What matters when hiring for pharma in Tamil Nadu

Pharma hiring in Tamil Nadu centres on a few clusters. The SIDCO pharmaceutical estate at Alathur, near Thiruporur in Chengalpattu district, houses API and formulation units. Gummidipoondi in Tiruvallur district, near the Andhra Pradesh border, has chemical and pharma plants. Chennai itself is a large hub for distributors, C&F agents and stockists, who need warehouse staff and pharmacists rather than chemists. Each cluster draws a different workforce.

Every production and quality role sits inside a GMP system. The revised Schedule M under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules raised expectations on training, documentation and data integrity. Interviewers therefore probe how candidates filled batch manufacturing records, handled deviations and worked in classified areas. QC analysts are tested on the instruments they claim, such as HPLC or dissolution testers. Pharmacists must hold current registration with the Tamil Nadu Pharmacy Council.

Plants with sterile or beta-lactam blocks need staff who follow gowning and segregation rules without being reminded. Shift work is common in production and utilities. Contract packing and stores staff must be enrolled in PF and ESI, and the OSH Code requires a licence for any contractor with 50 or more contract workers (as of Nov 2026). Auditors may also ask to see training records for contract staff.

What we check before sending candidates

  • Check B.Pharm, D.Pharm or M.Sc certificates against the role
  • Verify pharmacist registration with the Tamil Nadu Pharmacy Council
  • Ask QC candidates to explain their own HPLC or dissolution work
  • Review GMP training history and experience with batch records
  • Check boiler attendant certificates for utility operators

Pharma hiring: questions employers ask

Do you check pharmacist registration?

Yes. For any role that needs a registered pharmacist, we ask for the Tamil Nadu Pharmacy Council registration certificate and check that the renewal is current. Wholesale and retail drug licences depend on a qualified person being present, so a lapsed registration can put your licence at risk. A copy of the certificate goes with the profile.

Can you find QC analysts with regulatory audit experience?

We can search for them, though they are scarce and take longer to find than packing or production staff. Analysts who have faced USFDA, WHO-GMP or EU audits get frequent offers, so expect counter-offers. We test claims about instruments and audits in the screening call. Shortlist timing for standard roles is 48 hours for helpers and 7 days for skilled roles.

What fee do you charge for pharma hiring?

Pharma hiring is charged at [Lifeline's fee: to confirm]. For context only, permanent placement fees in the Indian market typically run from one to two months of the hire's annual pay, that is 8.33% to 16.67%, and specialist QA or regulatory roles sit toward the upper end. Contract staff are billed as wages plus statutory costs plus a service charge, with 18% GST, generally on the full invoice.

Can contract staff work in GMP areas?

Yes, if they are trained and documented like your own staff. Auditors look at training records, not employment type. Contract packing and stores staff need induction on GMP, hygiene and gowning before they enter a controlled area. We send candidates with basic awareness, and your QA team completes the site-specific training and sign-off.

What documents do you collect before a pharma joining?

We collect educational certificates, Pharmacy Council registration where relevant, the last three payslips, relieving letters, Aadhaar, PAN and bank details. For contract staff we also take nominee details for PF and ESI. Originals are seen at the interview, and your HR keeps copies under your own document control procedure.
